# Brand Ranking Page — Canonical Reference

**Purpose:** `all-protein-bar-brands.html` is fully generated by `build_brand_rankings.py`, not hand-written. This doc is the single source of truth for the ranking formula, category thresholds, and tier list, so a future session regenerates the page instead of re-deriving the methodology from scratch or hand-editing cards. Same spirit as `GUIDE_CRITERIA.md` for guide pages — see the Keto incident documented there for why this matters.

**To regenerate the page after `bars.js` changes:**
```
python3 build_brand_rankings.py
```
Run from the repo root. Then: (1) update `brands_manifest.json`'s `total_db_brand_count` if the brand count changed, (2) run `generate_brand_links.py`, (3) run the QA.md checklist, (4) diff against the previous version before uploading.

---

## The KYB Brand Score (locked 2026-08-10)

0-100 composite. Drives the page's 1-to-N rank directly — there is no manual override.

| Factor | Weight | What it measures |
|---|---|---|
| Ingredient quality | 60% | Average `ingredient_score` across every flavor the brand makes, min-max normalized against every brand's average in the current database |
| Protein efficiency | 25% | Average grams of protein per 100 calories, same normalization |
| Fiber | 15% | Average dietary fiber in grams, same normalization, capped at 100 |

**Deliberately excluded, and why:**
- **Price** — not tracked live, so it can't be part of a formula without going stale immediately.
- **Vitamins / fortification** — already tagged `neutral` (not positive or negative) in the ingredient-scoring schema itself (`score_insights` → `Fortified`). Scoring it as a plus in the composite would contradict the schema's own judgment on it.
- **Creatine / caffeine** — these are use-case and preference signals, not quality signals. A caffeinated bar isn't a "better" bar, it's a bar for a specific moment, and some people (pregnant, caffeine-sensitive, evening snackers) need to actively avoid it. Baking it into a universal score would silently claim "more caffeine = higher rank," which isn't a claim this site should make. These stay visible as badges on each card instead, so people can filter for or against them.

If this list changes, update this doc and the `brk-formula-note` copy on the page in the same session — don't let the code and the stated methodology drift apart.

## Category thresholds (locked 2026-08-10)

| Category | Rule |
|---|---|
| Protein First | avg protein per 100 cal &ge; 9 |
| Whole Food / High Fiber | avg fiber &ge; 6 AND not already Protein First |
| Solid Macro Profile | everything else (the default bucket — usually the majority of brands) |

## Distribution tiers — editorial, not data-derived

`bars.js` has no retail-distribution field. `WIDE` and `MID` are hand-curated brand-name sets living directly in `build_brand_rankings.py` (search for `WIDE = {` and `MID = {`). Anything not listed defaults to `"small"`. This is a real judgment call based on market knowledge, not a computed field — and the page says so explicitly in the `.brk-caveat` block at the bottom of the brand list. Don't remove that disclosure if you touch the copy.

When new brands land in `bars.js` (e.g. a batch of ~10 new brands), check whether any of them are genuinely widely-distributed before letting them default to "small" — the default is usually correct (most brands in this database are small DTC brands) but is worth a skim, not an assumption.

## Best-in-category picks and highlight/lowlight write-ups

Both are hand-picked brand names inside `build_brand_rankings.py` (`BEST_PICKS` and `HIGHLIGHT_BRANDS`), with the actual numbers in the prose pulled live from freshly computed stats — so re-running the script after a database update keeps the sentences numerically accurate even though the brand choices themselves are still editorial. If a named brand's data changes enough that the write-up stops making sense (e.g. it's no longer the category leader), that's a signal to swap in a new example, not just re-run the script and hope the prose still reads right — skim these six blurbs and six highlight cards after any significant database update.

## Per-brand card blurbs

Fully templated, not hand-written per brand (148 brands makes hand-writing unrealistic to maintain). Built from category, grade range, top positive/concern ingredient tags, and creatine/caffeine/fortification flags — see `blurb()` in `build_brand_rankings.py`. These read as data-generated summaries, which is intentional and stated nowhere as "editorial commentary" — don't oversell them as more subjective than they are.

## Bar Finder deep-link bug (fixed 2026-08-10) — don't reintroduce this

`app.js` resolves `?brand=` on `bar-finder.html` by slugifying every brand name in `BRAND_LIST` and matching against the raw URL param — the param itself is **not** slugified by app.js, so the link has to already be in slug form (`?brand=gryp`, not `?brand=Gryp` and not `?brand=Gryp+Bar`). The old `all-protein-bar-brands.html` linked with raw brand names and broke every single brand link on the page.

**Rule going forward:** any link to `bar-finder.html?brand=` must use `slugify(brand)` matching app.js's exact regex — lowercase, `[^a-z0-9]+` collapsed to a single hyphen, leading/trailing hyphens trimmed. `build_brand_rankings.py`'s `slugify()` function replicates this exactly and is verified (via a live Node script run against `app.js`'s own `slugify`) to produce 0 mismatches across all 148 brands, including tricky ones like `KIND` vs `KIND Protein Max`, trailing punctuation (`No Nuts!`), and apostrophes (`Jesse's WAKEUP!`). If any other page ever links to Bar Finder with a brand param, run it through the same slugify logic before shipping.
